title: Building with FPGAs and AI at uOttaHack
subtitle: uOttaHack · Fourth place in the FPGA category
paragraphs: In January, I travelled to Ottawa for uOttaHack. My team built K.A.R.E.N, a project combining FPGA hardware with an AI-powered interface.

We integrated services including ElevenLabs while exploring how software and programmable hardware could work together. I wanted more practical experience with FPGAs, so connecting one to a larger software system was a worthwhile challenge.
We placed fourth in the FPGA category. Given the time available, I was happy with what we managed to build and demonstrate.

Outside the competition, I enjoyed exploring Ottawa, visiting the University of Ottawa, and meeting students from other universities. It was interesting to compare their engineering communities with Guelph and Waterloo.
